articles.title: He conducido el Volkswagen ID. Polo: 5 cosas que me gustan y una que cambiaría
articles.standfirst: Tras conducirlo en Viena, ahora hemos vuelto a ponernos al volante en Valencia y eso nos ha permitido analizar qué aspectos nos gustan y cuáles mejoraríamos del nuevo Volkswagen ID. Polo
articles.summary: Tras conducirlo en Viena, ahora hemos vuelto a ponernos al volante en Valencia y eso nos ha permitido analizar qué aspectos nos gustan y cuáles mejoraríamos del nuevo Volkswagen ID. Polo
articles.body: Somos conscientes de que no se han espaciado mucho, pero el Volkswagen ID. Polo es uno de esos coches que necesitábamos conducir más de una vez para entender hasta qué punto ha cambiado la estrategia eléctrica de la marca alemana. Hace pocos días te hablábamos de nuestro primer encuentro con él por Viena, donde nos permitió conocer su comportamiento y comprobar que la nueva plataforma MEB+ había supuesto un avance importante. Ahora hemos vuelto a ponernos al volante, pero esta vez dentro de nuestras fronteras, concretamente en Valencia, para conducir la versión de 211 CV y batería de 52 kWh asociada al acabado Style. Una segunda prueba que nos ha dado para profundizar en algunos de los aspectos que pueden convertir a este coche en una de las novedades más relevantes de Volkswagen de los últimos años. Su importancia también afecta directamente a nuestro país, ya que el ID. Polo es el primer eléctrico de Volkswagen fabricado en España (lo hará en Martorell junto con el CUPRA Raval), y llega además manteniendo vigente una denominación que acumula más de 20 millones de unidades vendidas en medio siglo de historia. De ahí que para esta segunda toma de contacto nos hayamos querido centrar en ciertos aspectos que nos han llamado la atención, cinco para ser más precisos, al que sumamos otro que nos ha chirriado. La primera decisión acertada de Volkswagen ha sido no intentar que su nuevo utilitario eléctrico parezca un coche al margen de la gama como ya hizo con el resto de ID. Este ID. Polo mantiene unas proporciones reconocibles, conserva la carrocería de cinco puertas y utiliza un diseño bastante más cercano al de sus modelos tradicionales que al de esos primeros integrantes eléctricos. Estrena el lenguaje Pure Positive, desarrollado bajo la dirección de Andreas Mindt, con superficies laterales limpias, un frontal de líneas horizontales y unos pasos de rueda marcados que le proporcionan bastante anchura visual. Mide 4,05 metros de longitud, 1,82 de anchura y 1,53 de altura, por lo que sigue siendo un utilitario de clara vocación urbana pero con una presencia considerablemente más robusta que la del Polo de combustión. Ahí es donde entra uno de los detalles más interesantes de su diseño, que no es otro que el pilar C, cuya forma recupera una de las señas de identidad del primer Golf. También aparecen referencias clásicas en algunos diseños de llantas, disponibles en medidas de hasta 19 pulgadas, mientras la iluminación LED y los emblemas retroiluminados aportan la parte más moderna. Pero hay un elemento que merece una mención especial: el Retro Display. Al pulsar el botón View del volante, la instrumentación digital cambia sus gráficos para reproducir los relojes analógicos de un Golf de primera generación. A la izquierda aparece un velocímetro tradicional y, a su derecha, un supuesto cuentarrevoluciones que realmente indica la potencia entregada o recuperada por el sistema eléctrico. La pantalla multimedia también puede adoptar una presentación de los años setenta y ochenta, con una radio de aspecto analógico, un reproductor de casetes e incluso un indicador de batería que imita el nivel de combustible. Una solución especialmente atractiva que hará las delicias de los conductores que ya peinan canas y de los que, como un servidor, han empezado a entrar en la década de los 40. Volkswagen ha entendido que medio siglo de historia constituye un argumento comercial demasiado importante como para sustituirlo por una cifra (inicialmente se iba a llamar ID.2). El ID. Polo es el primer modelo de una nueva estrategia por la que los eléctricos irán recuperando denominaciones tradicionales, dejando atrás el sistema exclusivamente numérico con el que llegaron el ID.3, ID.4 o ID.7. La decisión también permite mantener una continuidad entre generaciones ya que el Polo de combustión seguirá comercializándose en paralelo al eléctrico, de manera que el cliente podrá identificar ambos como integrantes de una misma familia. La otra gran noticia está en su lugar de fabricación. El modelo ha sido desarrollado en Wolfsburg, pero se produce en Martorell junto al CUPRA Raval, dentro del proyecto de electrificación de las instalaciones españolas del Grupo Volkswagen. La planta catalana asume así la producción de un modelo especialmente relevante para el volumen comercial de Volkswagen, mientras que Pamplona fabricará el ID. Cross y el Škoda Epiq. Una transformación industrial importante que sitúa a España como centro de producción de los eléctricos pequeños del grupo. El habitáculo es otro de los apartados que reflejan cómo Volkswagen ha sabido evolucionar y corregir sus errores. La primera generación de eléctricos ID. introdujo soluciones que complicaban acciones cotidianas, desde los mandos táctiles del volante hasta el incómodo selector ‘Rear’ de los elevalunas. En el ID. Polo han desaparecido buena parte de esas decisiones. Ahora encontramos cuatro interruptores independientes para las ventanillas, botones físicos en el volante, una botonera específica para la climatización y un mando giratorio para el volumen. Es decir, que todo vuelve a ser como antes, sencillo de emplear y sin desviar constantemente la mirada de la carretera. Eso no significa que haya renunciado a la digitalización. Dispone de un cuadro de instrumentos de 10 pulgadas y una pantalla multimedia de 13 pulgadas, con una interfaz que durante nuestra prueba resultó infinitamente más rápida y fácil de manejar que la de los primeros ID. También ha mejorado la calidad percibida. Los ajustes, las tapicerías y la presentación transmiten más cuidado que en algunos de sus hermanos eléctricos, aunque todavía existen plásticos duros en las zonas menos visibles. Buena parte de los tejidos utiliza PET reciclado y el acabado Style incorpora materiales elaborados con hilo procedente de plástico marino recuperado. La segunda gran ventaja está en el espacio. La plataforma MEB+ concentra el motor y la transmisión en la parte delantera (siendo el primer ID en hacerlo), lo que permite utilizar un eje posterior especialmente compacto. Con 2,59 metros de batalla, el ID. Polo dispone de una segunda fila aprovechable para dos adultos y ofrece más longitud útil que el modelo térmico. Pero la cifra verdaderamente llamativa aparece un poco más atrás, ya que el maletero cubica nada menos que 441 litros. Esto supone un incremento de 90 litros frente a los 351 del Polo de combustión y, además, supera con holgura los 381 litros de un Golf convencional. Eso sí, la capacidad declarada incluye un amplio compartimento inferior muy útil para guardar los cables de recarga. Con los respaldos abatidos se alcanzan 1.243 litros. La versión que hemos conducido en Valencia desarrolla 211 CV y 290 Nm, acelera de 0 a 100 km/h en 7,1 segundos y pesa 1.576 kilos. Son unas cifras más que notables para un utilitario de estas características, aunque lo que más convence es la manera en que Volkswagen ha ajustado la entrega de potencia. El acelerador responde con progresividad y evita esa salida excesivamente brusca que encontramos en determinados eléctricos. El ID. Polo tiene fuerza de sobra para adelantar, pero resulta fácil dosificarla incluso al acelerar pronto después de una curva. La dirección responde con precisión alrededor del punto central y el chasis permite enlazar curvas sin movimientos excesivos. No ofrece una comunicación especialmente rica cuando se fuerza el ritmo, pero se comporta de forma natural y mantiene esa combinación de confort, estabilidad y facilidad de conducción que esperamos de un utilitario europeo bien afinado. La suspensión utiliza McPherson delante y un eje torsional detrás. Volkswagen ha trabajado específicamente los amortiguadores, anclajes y elementos de aislamiento para esta nueva arquitectura eléctrica, consiguiendo una absorción convincente sin perjudicar el control de la carrocería. También merece reconocimiento el nuevo equipo de frenos, con discos en las cuatro ruedas y un sistema que combina regeneración y fricción mecánica. El pedal ofrece una respuesta bastante más convencional que en muchos eléctricos, especialmente cuando se realiza una frenada progresiva. En resumidas cuentas, no estamos ante el típico coche urbano blando y que transmite poco, el ID. Polo se comporta como lo que es y ha sido siempre, un utilitario europeo equilibrado, con una pisada noble y un muy buen aplomo. Volkswagen ha conseguido que el ID. Polo sea su eléctrico de acceso tanto por tamaño como por precio, con el objetivo de conseguir lo que logró el modelo original en su momento, acercarse al pueblo y democratizar la movilidad, eléctrica en este caso. De ahí que el listado de precios sea agresivo y se mueva próximo a lo que la firma prometió en su momento de ofrecer un vehículo por debajo de los 25.000 euros. En este sentido, el ID. Polo Match de 116 CV cuesta 25.990 euros sin ayudas ni descuentos que, una vez aplicados (combinando las promociones de la marca, financiación mediante Volkswagen Financial Services, Plan Auto+ y las condiciones asociadas a los Certificados de Ahorro Energético), reducen la tarifa a nada menos que 17.900 euros. Con todo la gama queda configurada de la siguiente manera: ID.Polo Life 116 CV 28.860 euros (19.100 euros) ID. Polo Life 211 CV 35.070 euros (23.900 euros) ID. Polo Style 135 CV 33.900 euros (22.800 euros) ID. Polo Style 211 CV 38.920 euros (27.500 euros) De esta forma, el ID. Polo entra con argumentos en un segmento donde tendrá que enfrentarse al Renault 5 E-Tech, al Citroën ë-C3 y a los fabricantes chinos, especialmente BYD con el Dolphin Surf. La diferencia es que Volkswagen puede ofrecer ahora una versión de acceso relativamente asequible y otra de 211 CV y hasta 449 kilómetros que permite utilizar el coche como vehículo principal, a la espera del ID.Polo GTI. No todo iban a ser alabanzas y este ID. Polo cuenta también con algunas carencias que merecen ser dichas. La primera, la recarga. Si bien la nueva plataforma MEB+ ha mejorado considerablemente la eficiencia, Volkswagen ha sido conservadora con la recarga. La batería LFP de 37 kWh admite 88 kW en corriente continua, mientras que la NMC de 52 kWh alcanza 105 kW. Los tiempos del 10 al 80% son de aproximadamente 23 y 24 minutos, respectivamente. No son malos registros porque las baterías tienen una capacidad contenida, aunque una potencia superior habría mejorado las posibilidades de viaje de las versiones de mayor autonomía. Especialmente cuando varios competidores ya están trabajando con sistemas de carga considerablemente más potentes. No obstante, si lo vemos como un coche para el día a día, esta característica no será tan representativa. Tampoco termina de convencerme la ausencia de levas de regeneración detrás del volante. El ID. Polo estrena una conducción One Pedal real que permite detener el vehículo al levantar completamente el acelerador, seleccionando la posición B, pero unas levas permitirían modificar la retención con mayor rapidez sin recurrir al selector de marcha. Para circular por ciudad, el sistema actual funciona correctamente; en carretera, preferiría disponer de esa posibilidad de ajuste. La configuración mecánica también deja algunas dudas. Entre los 116 y los 135 CV apenas hay una diferencia relevante de prestaciones para determinados compradores, mientras que después aparece un salto considerable hasta los 211 CV. Habría tenido sentido ofrecer una opción intermedia con la batería grande para quien quiera más autonomía sin necesidad de llegar a esa potencia. Más que nada porque con 15 CV más se ofertará el ID. Polo GTI que si bien tendrá un ajuste específico, en lo que a rendimiento se refiere queda muy próximo al probado. De ahí que una alternativa de 190 CV hubiera cubierto mejor la gama. Por último, hay una cuestión que merece cierta reflexión: Volkswagen presenta el ID. Polo como una manera de democratizar el coche eléctrico, pero ya había recorrido ese camino con el e-Up!. El pequeño eléctrico llegó en 2013 y, tras su actualización de 2019, ofrecía hasta 260 kilómetros de autonomía con un precio para aquel momento de 22.570 euros antes de campañas y ayudas, que se reducía a 20.290 euros con descuentos comerciales. Era un automóvil más pequeño, sencillo y económico de fabricar, pensado precisamente para resolver los desplazamientos cotidianos. El ID. Polo es objetivamente más completo: ofrece cinco plazas, mucho más maletero, mayor autonomía y una capacidad de viajar que el e-Up! no tenía. Pero también obliga a desembolsar 25.990 euros antes de incentivos para acceder a la gama. Volkswagen habría podido mantener aquella estrategia de un urbano eléctrico realmente pequeño y asequible y complementarla ahora con este Polo. En lugar de eso, ha dejado un hueco por debajo que están aprovechando fabricantes como Dacia y algunos constructores chinos. Sea como fuere, después de volver a conducirlo, el ID. Polo me parece un producto muy bien resuelto por diseño, espacio, ergonomía y comportamiento. Ha recuperado cualidades que Volkswagen había perdido parcialmente en sus primeros eléctricos y ofrece una versión de 211 CV con suficiente autonomía para asumir el papel de coche único.

articles.title: Dilpreet Singh's four-goal show headlines India's 13-1 rout of Indonesia at Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's men's hockey team made a commanding start to their Asian Games title defence, cruising past Indonesia 13-1 in their opening Pool A encounter o.
articles.body: India's men's hockey team made a commanding start to their Asian Games title defence, cruising past Indonesia 13-1 in their opening Pool A encounter on Sunday.Dilpreet Singh was the standout performer, finding the net four times as the defending champions produced a dominant display. Shilanand Lakra and Sukhjeet Singh chipped in with two goals apiece, while Abhishek, Rajinder Singh, Mandeep Singh, Harmanpreet Singh and Jugraj Singh were also on target.Indonesia managed a consolation goal through Aulia Al Ardh in the 33rd minute, but India remained firmly in control for most of the contest.The defending champions needed only six minutes to open the scoring. Harmanpreet's drag flick was kept out by Indonesian goalkeeper Alam Fajar, but Lakra reacted quickest to score from the rebound.Abhishek then doubled India's advantage in the 12th minute, again finishing off a rebound after Fajar had saved the initial effort.Dilpreet took over from there. He made it 3-0 in the 18th minute after converting an assist from Abhishek before finding the net again just a minute later, guiding Sukhjeet's pass home from the far post.India's relentless attacking pressure continued as Rajinder Singh scored from another rebound following a fine attacking move involving Sukhjeet. Mandeep Singh then added another field goal two minutes later to put India 6-0 ahead.The Indians had an opportunity to extend their lead further in the 27th minute when Manpreet Singh was fouled inside the 'D' while attempting to convert a rebound. Harmanpreet stepped up for the resulting penalty stroke, but Fajar made a save with his outstretched right leg.Harmanpreet, however, did not have to wait long for his goal. He converted a penalty corner in the following minute to give India a 7-0 advantage at half-time.Indonesia finally found a breakthrough three minutes into the second half. Al Ardh converted a penalty corner in the 33rd minute to give his side a consolation goal.India quickly resumed their assault. Lakra scored his second of the match in the 35th minute after receiving a well-weighted pass from Rajinder.Dilpreet completed his hat-trick two minutes later, pouncing on a rebound after Fajar had blocked the initial attempt.Sukhjeet then joined the scoring spree in the 38th minute, finding the net with a field goal to make it 10-1.Jugraj Singh converted India's next penalty corner in the 47th minute before Sukhjeet struck again a minute later to complete his brace.Dilpreet saved his best for last, adding his fourth goal in the 49th minute to complete India's 13-1 victory.India will next face Sri Lanka on Tuesday.The match also marked the first Asian Games appearance of India's new primary saffron kits. Despite Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey's earlier claim that both Indian teams would wear their traditional blue jerseys at the Games, the men's and women's sides have instead turned out in the saffron kits first worn during the recent World Cup in the Netherlands and Belgium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luke Littler could boycott Dutch events because of booing
articles.summary: Luke Littler threatens a boycott of playing in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
articles.body:
World champion Luke Littler has threatened to stop playing in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The referee stopped the match during his narrow win against Nathan Aspinall in the last eight on Saturday to warn the hostile crowd about its behaviour, before play resumed.

It followed Littler also being booed during his win against home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday.

Littler has faced similar treatment in Germany and has stopped playing in European Tour events in the country.

Asked if he was prepared to take a similar stance for Dutch events, the 19-year-old told Online Darts: "100%."

Littler, who is expected to play at the European Championship in Dortmund in October, added: "With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same.

"If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro tours over there. There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I'm getting booed.

"I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing, I've just walked off stage and not thanked anyone. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

Littler was also booed during a win over Rob Cross at the PDC World Championship in December.

After the match, he said: "I'm not bothered [by the booing]. Really not bothered. You guys pay for tickets and you pay for my prize so thanks for booing me."

articles.title: Asian Games: Smriti Mandhana breaks T20 record as India beat Bangladesh
articles.summary: India defeat Bangladesh by 114 runs to book women’s cricket final against Sri Lanka, who beat Pakistan by eight wickets.
articles.body:
Smriti Mandhana has become the highest run-scorer in women’s T20 international cricket, guiding India to a crushing win over Bangladesh in an Asian Games semifinal in Japan.

The recently crowned Asian champions defeated Bangladesh by 114 runs on Sunday as Mandhana’s fellow opener Shafali Verma hit her maiden T20 hundred at the Korogi Athletic Park ground in Nagoya.

Mandhana scored 37 off 19 balls with five fours and two sixes in her side’s 195-4 in 20 overs and, in the process, went past New Zealand all-rounder Suzie Bates’s 4,758 runs at the top of the all-time list to stand on 4,788 runs from 171 innings.

Earlier this month, Mandhana reached the top of overall run-scoring charts in women’s international cricket after smashing a record-breaking 124 off 64 balls in the Women’s Asia Cup in Dubai.

Mandhana overtook former India captain Mithali Raj , who had been the top international scorer with 10,868 international runs, during her match-winning innings against Hong Kong on Thursday.

Verma was the star on the day for India in the Asian Games semifinal, scoring 100 not out off 49 balls with three fours and nine sixes. She reached her hundred off the final ball of the 20-over innings and was clearly emotional as she took off her helmet and raised her bat in celebration towards her applauding teammates on the boundary.

India then restricted Bangladesh to 81 in 15.4 overs.

The 50-over world champions will meet Sri Lanka on Tuesday in the gold medal match, which will be a replay of the Asia Cup final from last Sunday, when India won a record-extending eighth title.

Sri Lanka advanced to the final after their captain Chamari Athapaththu led them to an easy eight-wicket win over Pakistan with more than two overs to spare.

The island nation hunted down the 178-run target with 13 balls to spare as Athapaththu led the scoring with 83 not out.

Earlier, Pakistan were asked to bat first and, with half-centuries from Ayesha Zafar and Shawaal Zulfiqar, they posted a total of 177-4 in 20 overs.

Zafar, who hit the joint third-fastest fifty for Pakistan in WT20Is off 27 balls, shared a record stand of 115 with Zulfiqar, which is the second-highest in the format for Pakistan and the highest for the third wicket.

Pakistan were able to score 27 runs off the last three overs as their all-rounder captain Fatima Sana hit two fours and one six in her 12-ball 20.

In reply, Sana broke Sri Lanka’s 36-run opening stand in the fifth over, bowling out Imesha Dulani for 27. Athapaththu, who hit seven fours and six sixes in her 50-ball knock, joined forces with Hasini Perera (42) to form a match-winning 95-run partnership off 56 balls.

Nashra Sundhu provided Pakistan the breakthrough in the 14th over, with Sri Lanka requiring another 47 runs off the last six overs, but Athapaththu’s quickfire stand of 47 off 23 balls with Harshitha Samrawickrama (17 not out) took their team over the line with 13 balls to spare.

Pakistan will play Bangladesh for the bronze medal, also on Tuesday.

articles.title: Salah scores hat-trick as Trabzonspor beat Galatasaray in Turkish league

articles.body:
Mohamed ‌‌‌‌Salah scored a hat-trick and provided an assist as Trabzonspor thrashed defending champions Galatasaray 4-0 at home, handing the ⁠⁠⁠⁠Istanbul side their first defeat of the Turkish Super Lig season.

Salah opened the ⁠⁠⁠⁠scoring in the fourth minute on Saturday, running through from midfield and finishing calmly, before turning provider to set up Noah Saviolo, who struck from ‌‌‌‌inside the penalty area in the 39th minute.

Salah added a third in the 44th minute with a clinical finish from a Franculino Dju assist, sending the team he joined last month into the break three goals ⁠⁠⁠⁠up.

He completed his hat-trick ⁠⁠⁠⁠in the 80th minute, running more than half the length of the pitch unchallenged to score with a trademark ⁠⁠⁠⁠side-foot finish.

The Egyptian icon has scored seven goals in six appearances in the league this season, with two assists to his name as well.

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk was sent to the stands in ⁠⁠⁠⁠the 71st minute, while ⁠⁠⁠⁠Lesley Ugochukwu was shown a red card in the 87th minute.

German coach Thomas Reis took charge of Trabzonspor this week ‌‌‌‌following the departure of Fatih Tekke earlier this month.

Trabzonspor are fifth in the table with ‌‌‌‌10 ‌‌‌‌points from six games, three points behind leaders Galatasaray.

articles.title: Two silvers, one agonising miss: Elavenil Valarivan reveals what went wrong as late lapse costs her Asian Games shooting gold
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Elavenil Valarivan walked away from the Asian Games shooting range with two silver medals on Sunday, but there was also a nagging sense of .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Elavenil Valarivan walked away from the Asian Games shooting range with two silver medals on Sunday, but there was also a nagging sense of what might have been after the Indian shooter let a commanding lead slip away in the final stages of the women’s 10m air rifle individual event.The 27-year-old had looked firmly on course for gold after building a lead of nearly 1.5 points, but three loose shots towards the end changed the complexion of the final. Japan’s Taichi Hinata eventually held her nerve to win gold with an Asian Games record 253.0, while Elavenil settled for silver with 252.4. South Korea’s Ban Hyojin took bronze with 230.4.“I did get a bit relaxed. I think I really need to work on my finals some more,” Elavenil said after the final.“I knew that I was in the top three. Although I was coming back to focusing on my process and my technique, I did get a bit relaxed. Once the medal was assured, the pressure was released. It was more about me getting a little easy on my process,” she added.From gold in sight to another silverElavenil was still only 0.3 points behind Hinata heading into the final two shots. She managed 10.4 against the Japanese shooter’s 10.6, with the deficit increasing to 0.5. Elavenil then shot 10.1 with her final attempt, while Hinata responded with 10.2 to seal gold by 0.6 points.Rather than dwell on the missed opportunity, Elavenil viewed the experience as another lesson.“I felt I gave my absolute best,” she said. “I think it is all a learning process.”“Post-Paris, it has been like this, and I am very grateful that I have been getting a lot of opportunities to learn and experiment and utilise my potential to my absolute best,” she said.The silver was her second medal of the day after she had earlier combined with Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod to win silver in the women’s 10m air rifle team event. The Indian trio finished with 1898 points, behind gold medallists China, while Japan were fourth.Elavenil was India’s standout performer in the team competition, scoring 633.5 to qualify for the individual final. Sonam also made the final and finished sixth with 167.0.Two silvers, a medal milestoneThe double silver marked a significant milestone for Elavenil, who had waited eight years for an Asian Games medal after making her debut at Jakarta 2018.“The first conversation me and my coach were having was that it has been eight years since my first Asian Games to my second,” she said.“It was more about being very grateful that I was getting the opportunity to be a part of the contingent and represent my country.”Her coach Neha Chavan was not in Nagoya, but had sent her a message before the competition: “You have trained your absolute best. There’s nothing more you can do on this given day. All I would wish for you is to follow the technique, trust yourself and be courageous, as you’ve always been.”“I’m very grateful that I’ve got her by my side all the time, even when she is not there,” Elavenil said.The two medals also offered an early boost to India’s shooting campaign. “I think it is going to boost the entire team. Knowing that on the first day we have done two medals, going on from here, I think it is just on,” she said.And after the disappointment of missing gold, her immediate priority was refreshingly simple.“I think next is going to be rest and recovery. I’m missing my bed terribly,” she said, laughing. “I just want to get back and celebrate it with my coaches and my teammates.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bron Breakker and 9 More WWE, AEW Superstars Who Are Way Better as Heels
articles.summary: While there will always be characters who live in the gray area, the foundation of professional wrestling is built on the concept of good vs. evil.
articles.body:
While there will always be characters who live in the gray area, the foundation of professional wrestling is built on the concept of good vs. evil.

In most feuds, there is a heroic babyface and a villainous heel, and for the most part, the fans usually follow these roles and react accordingly.

Of course, there are exceptions to this rule. We've seen plenty of heels be cheered because fans just love them too much to boo, like Stone Cold Steve Austin, and then there are faces who receive tons of boos, much like The Rock did early in his WWE run before turning heel to join The Nation of Domination.

Some Superstars just operate better on one side of the fence than the other, and there are many who have made an entire career out of being the good or bad guy.

Let's take a look at some of the WWE and AEW stars who seem best suited for the heel role.

There is no denying the physical ability of Bron Breakker, and for a long time, he was a huge babyface in NXT, but he has definitely found his footing as a heel on the main roster.

Part of what makes him so good as a villain is his believable intensity. When he stares an opponent in the eye and gets that crazed look on his face, you get the genuine feeling that he could snap at any moment.

That kind of convincing heel work can carry a Superstar a long way, but when you add in his athletic ability, you have the recipe for someone who could be a top heel for many years.

His current storyline with The Vision might see him turn face, but there is a good chance he ends up turning back to the dark side before too long.

Throughout the entirety of his WWE run, Ricochet was a babyface who was often associated with superheroes due to his ridiculous athleticism and agility.

Shortly after arriving in AEW, Tony Khan turned him heel, and suddenly it feels like we are seeing an entirely different performer in front of us.

Ricochet has been incredibly entertaining as a cocky, smarmy little jerk who often relies on his much stronger allies to do the dirty work for him.

And on top of that, it looks like he is having the most fun he has had in years as a pro wrestler. When the performer is enjoying themselves, it makes it much easier for fans to invest in their character.

This might be one of the most obvious choices on the list, but Logan Paul is only really suited to playing a heel in WWE.

Even if WWE tried to turn him babyface, there is a big portion of the crowd who would refuse to cheer simply because of who he is.

In fact, it's not just his character that a lot of people dislike. It's him as a person, and in many cases, that can be just as valuable to a promoter.

Having someone who fans genuinely want to see lose is important, and nobody in WWE fits the bill better than The Social Media Megastar.

When it comes to AEW, Jon Moxley is among the most popular stars on the roster, especially with the hardcore fans of the promotion, but he definitely works best as an antagonist.

Much like Breakker, it comes down to his believability. Mox is great at using words and facial expressions to appear unhinged, and he is just as good at being a bully in the ring.

When he faces Will Ospreay for the men's world title at All Out, it wouldn't be surprising to see the crowd split between the two, but Mox will undoubtedly be the villain in this story.

He can still work as a babyface, but he offers so much more value as a heel, especially with a group of talented wrestlers like The Death Riders behind him.

Most of the women in WWE can jump between being a face and heel with no issues, but Nia Jax is one who seems tailor-made for being the antagonist.

Not only does she seem to work better in that role with her personality, but her size and power advantage make her almost impossible to book as the underdog in any situation.

Jax had a short run as a babyface, and while it worked fine at the time, she has settled into her role as a heel and embraced it.

Her tag team with Lash Legend has been good for both women, but Jax could easily be slotted back into the world title scene at any time because she can be a dominant heel against anyone on the roster.

The women's division in AEW has a lot of great heels and faces, but nobody holds a candle to the CEO when it comes to being the villain.

Mercedes Mone is so good at what she does that a lot of people cheer for her anyway, even if she is facing someone they want to see win over her.

Her run in AEW, NJPW and on the indies saw her accumulate so many belts that she gave herself the nickname Ultimo Mone, referencing the famous picture of Ultimo Dragon holding several title belts at once.

She looks like she is having the time of her life playing a heel, so there is no reason why it should change anytime soon.

Dominik Mysterio came into WWE as a bland second-generation babyface who was teaming with his dad, the legendary Rey Mysterio. As soon as WWE turned him heel and gave him the chance to show some personality, he began to thrive.

Joining Judgment Day and becoming a backstabbing jerk gave fans a chance to see what he could do on his own, away from his father's huge shadow.

Since then, Dom has been a tag team champion, the men's intercontinental champion, and AAA mega champion, and he has been in on-screen relationships with Rhea Ripley and Liv Morgan.

Dirty Dom has established himself as a great heel, and if he continues along the path he is on, it would not be surprising to see him in the world title picture within the next couple of years.

When MJF talks about being one of the best talkers, best workers and best all-around talents in pro wrestling, he's not lying, and that's what makes him such an effective heel.

The former AEW world champion backs up everything he says, and despite taking the low road in many situations, he has also proved he can get the job done on his own several times.

When someone you don't like talks trash and it's all based on facts and reality, it makes you want to punch them in the face even more, and that is part of what makes MJF so special.

Even the fans who love him also love seeing him lose because he is so good at putting others over when the time comes to do it. He is a rare talent, and at only 30 years old, he could potentially be a top heel for many years to come.

Randy Orton has reached the point in his career where fans will cheer for him whether he is the good or bad guy, but he has always been much more interesting as a heel.

The RKO out of nowhere is the perfect move to use on unsuspecting babyfaces, but where the Viper really thrives is his character work.

His promos, facial expressions and the way he wrestles all suit him as an antagonist, and the fact that he is bigger than most of the roster makes it easy for him to bully people, too.

Having him return to his roots as a villain as he chases world title no. 15 was the best decision WWE could have made for him.

Chris Jericho might be considered the kind of reinventing himself after having so many different versions of his character over the years, but the most successful rebranding of a veteran in AEW might just be Christian Cage.

Making jokes about everyone's dad has made him one of the funnier people in the company, and wrestling in a sleeveless turtleneck is the kind of thing you don't think will work until someone like him does it.

His current tag team run with Adam Copeland is bound to come to an end eventually, but the best part of it has been how Copeland has remained a babyface while Cage hasn't changed a single thing about himself to fit in. He is still the same arrogant heel he has been for the past few years.

Everyone listed here has proven they operate better as a heel in WWE and AEW, but they are not the only ones. Who do you think are some of the most natural villains in either company?

articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs defensive back L'Jarius Sneed spoke with reporters on Friday. He reflected on his first official game back with the team and his immediate impact.

"It was a great start, but go back and watch the film," said Sneed, "and know that we've got a whole lot of work to do. We've been after it each and every day."

In his first game since returning to Kansas City this season, Sneed led the team with eight tackles (seven solo). He credits training camp with getting him and his teammates on the same page and focused to be dogs defensively.

"I would say it comes from training camp," said Sneed. "Training camp teaches us how to be dogs and change our mentality."

During Sneed's first tenure with the Chiefs, he appeared in 57 regular-season games, tallying ten interceptions and 40 passes defended.

articles.title: Jordan's Review: Auburn Tigers can't keep up with Florida Gators
articles.summary: Phillip Jordan discusses Auburn's defensive struggles and the offense's inability to keep up with Florida on Saturday night.
articles.body:
On Saturday night, the Auburn Tigers could not keep up with the Florida Gators and dropped their first game of the season 44-39 . It is too early in the season to label this game as a must-win entering Saturday, but for Auburn , an opposite result would have set them up for potentially seven or eight wins. Now the Tigers have questions to answer after their first loss of the season.

The defense was the storyline following the loss on Saturday night. Auburn gave up 495 total yards to Florida, with 252 through the air and 243 on the ground. The Gators also controlled the game with time of possession, holding the ball for 39:16 versus Auburn's 20:44. Now, Auburn does what to play with pace, but the Tigers' defense was on the field way too much in the game. The lack of defense made Florida quarterback Aaron Philo look like a veteran SEC quarterback in the game. He was 15 of 22 for 204 yards and one touchdown. The team had zero answers for Gators running back Jaden Baugh, who put up 162 yards and three touchdowns. For any chance at a win, Auburn had to limit his production.

Another key statistic was that the Gators were 7 of 15 on third down, and they were perfect on three fourth-down attempts. When it mattered the most, the Auburn defense could not get off the field to give the ball back to the offense. Florida averaged 11 yards per pass attempt and consistently made big plays in the passing game. Adjustments will need to be made in the secondary for this team moving forward. Even in the win over Baylor to open the season, Bears quarterback D.J. Lagway passed for 333 yards in the game.

On the offensive side of the ball, it is evident that the offensive line is still an issue. Byrum Brown was sacked seven times in the game, and Auburn could not get the rushing game going with the running backs. Jeremiah Cobb and Bryson Washington had only 40 yards on 12 carries, with Cobb getting the one touchdown. The carries number was low due to two factors: not possessing the ball much and then getting behind by 17 points in the second half. For the rest of the season, Auburn is going to need to find a way to be more successful in the traditional run game.

It was not all negative for Auburn in the loss. This team on offense did show a lot of fight at the end and continued to put pressure on the Florida offense. Brown did have a rough start in the first quarter with an interception, but overall, he had a solid individual performance. Brown passed for 271 yards and three touchdowns, with the final one to Chas Nimrod to give Auburn a chance with an onside kick with 24 seconds remaining. Brown was the leading rusher with 65 yards and one touchdown.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from Oklahoma's Week 3 win over New Mexico
articles.summary: 3 takeaways after the Oklahoma Sooners defeat the New Mexico Lobos.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners have completed the non-league portion of their 2026 schedule with a 2-1 record. OU got a home win over the New Mexico Lobos on Saturday night, prevailing with a 14-6 victory in a game that was ugly from start to finish.

Head coach Brent Venables and the Sooners now head to SEC play, and they have to be feeling less than stellar after a rocky win. After last week's disappointing loss to Michigan , the hope was that Oklahoma would show improved execution and put the Lobos away early. That didn't happen, as head coach Jason Eck's New Mexico team hung in until the very end.

For this week's takeaways, we'll start with the positive, move to the somewhat frustrating, and end with the extremely bad. Here are three takeaways from OU's win over New Mexico.

Where would Oklahoma be without their defense? Seriously, the Sooners needed every ounce of what they got defensively to beat New Mexico, and after some uneven performances through the first two weeks, it was a pretty sound operation on that side of the ball for OU. Despite being repeatedly put in bad situations by their offense, the Oklahoma defense allowed just six points, had six sacks, and limited UNM to 96 rushing yards.

Despite missing key players like Kip Lewis , Cole Sullivan , and Michael Boganowski, the Sooners tackled better against the Lobos and only gave up a handful of chunk plays. Most of those plays came on New Mexico's final drive, when Oklahoma was absolutely spent. Still, the Sooners got one more stop to close things out.

One of OU's three phases showed up on Saturday night, and it looks like the defense will be asked to carry an impossibly heavy load for the rest of the season.

One of the more surprising parts of Saturday's game was the fact that OU struggled on special teams. Between Isaiah Sategna III muffing a punt and Tate Sandell missing a very makeable field goal, something that is usually a big positive for the Sooners was a negative against New Mexico.

It's pretty simple for OU's special teams going forward. With the razor-thin margins that offensive incompetence will give the Sooners in SEC games, Oklahoma will have to win the special teams battle each week if they want a chance to win conference games. What happened on Saturday night can't happen again, or OU will lose games like this.

Okay, let's talk about it. For the second time in their three years as an SEC member, the Sooners do not field a functional offense. The school that has always been at the forefront of offensive football cannot do anything right on that side of the ball, again. OU already made a change at offensive coordinator and got a new quarterback after the 2024 season, and the offense has still landed here, despite that.

There's just nothing the Sooners can consistently count on when they have the ball. After a week of the fanbase begging for a commitment to the run game, Oklahoma averaged just 1.9 yards per carry. That's 32 attempts for 61 yards against a Mountain West defense. The passing game wasn't much better, as quarterback John Mateer threw two bad interceptions, despite also tossing two touchdowns.

Oklahoma struggles along the offensive line, currently has one reliable wide receiver, doesn't have anything resembling a normal running back rotation, has a quarterback that is being asked to do everything, and has an offensive play-caller in Ben Arbuckle who seems to have no idea what the unit's identity is going to be. Aside from the tight end room, everything seems to have taken a step back from last year.

There don't appear to be any answers for OU's offense, either in the short or long term. In the short term, it's imperative that the Sooners find something, anything, they can do well on Saturdays and build around. The bar is that low right now. In the long-term, Oklahoma absolutely must figure out a way to play offensive football under Venables. Complementary football has eluded OU for nearly a decade, and everyone inside the building's jobs will hinge on their ability to make that happen for once.

The 2026 Sooners have no more tune-ups. The SEC is here, and Oklahoma now gets the top two teams in America in the next two games. OU will get embarrassed against Georgia and Texas unless they engineer a massive turnaround on offense. This week was the opportunity to get things right, and clearly nothing has changed. Oklahoma has to figure it out, or it'll be an ugly season in Norman.

articles.title: Position Grades: Buffalo
articles.summary: Let’s grade yesterday’s Buffalo beatdown
articles.body:
As expected, Penn State dominated and covered the spread against a hopelessly overmatched Buffalo squad. But, how did the performance itself grade out? Let's find out!

It felt like a hot and cold performance for Rocco Becht . On the one hand, he still had his inexplicable moments of running out of bounds when being chased and losing yards instead of just throwing the damn ball away, not to mention he locked in so hard on Koby Howard in the red zone when Howard was double covered instead of firing to a wide open Chase Sowell in the middle of the end zone for an easy pitch-and-catch touchdown. On the other hand, he had some awesome moments like finding Koby for a 70-yard TD strike along with some other downfield shots. Given that he threw for 212 yards and a pair of TD's with no turnovers, it's hard to ding him too much. Alex Manske did a serviceable job in backup duty as well, as he continues to get back up to speed with game experience.

You wanted explosive runs? You got them! Quinton Martin led the way with a 61-yard dash that he would've housed, had the turf monster not tripped him up around the 10-yard line. Cam Wallace also had a lovely 59-yard scamper to the end zone. Meanwhile, James Peoples racked up a pair of TD's, as he showed more decisiveness and vision than he had in the first two games. Carson Hansen to his credit, did have a nice scamper to the end zone later in the game, but I think the "RB1" title should belong to Martin or Peoples at this point.

In addition to racking up another 100-plus yard receiving performance (115), Koby also took a 20-yard reverse to the house for his second of two TD's on the day. Chase also made an amazing leaping grab on a jump ball thrown by Becht for 35 yards, and Brett Eskildsen also caught a couple balls for 24 yards. That being said, there were a few too many drops from this group at one point when the offense hit a lull for a few straight drives in the second quarter, so I'm gonna have to ding them half a grade.

Andrew Rappleyea had a TD catch and later on was forced to leave the game favoring his right arm. Thankfully, it sounds like it's nothing that will keep him out of game action going forward, according to Matt Campbell's post game presser. Shout-out to Finn Furmanek who had an awesome 31-yard catch late in the game.

Vaea Ikakoula had some snapping issues substituting under center for Brock Riker, who only played the first couple of series before sitting the remainder of the game. Other than that, the running backs typically had lanes to run through and Becht had time to scan the field and find an open receiver.

Caleb Bacon forced a fumble, which Ike Ezeogu pounced on. PSU would ultimately cash in on said fumble recovery to take a 17-0 lead just nine minutes into the game and never looked back. The entire front seven did a good job for the most part not allowing Buffalo to get any sort of rhythm going offensively. Buffalo was held to 173 total offensive yards, with 113 of them on the ground, many of them being earned later in the game when it was all second and third-string guys on defense for the Nittany Lions . I would have liked to seen a sack from the group, so going with an A-minus here.

Kooper Ebel continues to impress at linebacker, garnering a team-high five tackles and a sack. Alex Tatsch also saw plenty of action, picking up four tackles himself. Much like the D-line, the linebackers did a good job of keeping the Buffalo ground game in check when it mattered.

Buffalo only garnered 60 total yards of passing, despite coming into the game with their top receiver Chance Morrow averaging nine receptions and over 100 yards and two TD's per game. That's a testament to the blanket coverage the secondary provided. Marcus Neal forced a fumble, which he recovered and PSU also cashed in for six on their subsequent drive.

I predicted going into this game that Zay Robinson would take a punt or kickoff return back for a TD, and on his first punt return, he came damn close to making me look like a genius. Zay returned a whopping eight Buffalo punts for 109 total yards, one of the best single-game punt returning performances since Daequan Hardy set a program record 129 yards against UMass in 2023. Ryan Barker nailed a 48-yard field goal to open up the scoring and later added a chip shot one, so I think it's safe to say he's fine. Nathan Tiyce had a less than stellar punt that gave Buffalo starting field position close to midfield and ultimately led to a Bulls' field goal, but he did pin them inside their own red zone once again.

The staff really emphasized getting the running game going this week, and delivered. The offensive lull in the second quarter and some of the red zone offense issues were more due to poor execution, as opposed to questionable play calling. They also did a good job of getting a big enough lead early on to get all of their starters out by mid-third quarter.

Some folks might complain about the defense garnering several penalties, but most of them were very ticky-tack and probably shouldn't have been called. Each of Buffalo's scoring drives relied upon said penalties helping move the chains, because they sure weren't capable of doing it on their own.

articles.title: Mercedes draws the line in Antonelli-Russell battles: 'That was a bit beyond'
articles.summary: Mercedes would prefer the battles between Kimi Antonelli and George Russell to resemble those in Monza rather than Montreal. Speaking on the NU Silver Arrows...
articles.body:
Mercedes would prefer the battles between Kimi Antonelli and George Russell to resemble those in Monza rather than Montreal.

Speaking on the NU Silver Arrows Radio Show, Mercedes' Trackside Engineering Director, Andrew Shovlin , addressed the battles Antonelli and Russell have had throughout the 2026 season so far.

According to the Briton, what happened in Montreal earlier this season between the teammates was over the limit they would prefer to see on the pit wall and in the garage.

He began: "For us, Monza was an easier watch than Canada. Canada felt like it was, a bit beyond the level that we want our two to race at. But as I said, it's so easy to stop them racing, but we've barely ever interfered. We just let them know what we want to see.

Shovlin highlighted that if the drivers follow the rules, they will not interfere with team orders.

"And if they give us that, then they're free to race. As I said, probably the best thing for the Constructors' Championship, but for both championships is they go into every weekend thinking they've got a chance to win, the team will support them in doing that and that will help them bring their very best to the track each weekend."

Antonelli going wide in Monza - Photo: Race Pictures

Shovlin looks ahead to the Azerbaijan GP: What's possible for Mercedes?

Mercedes expects to perform better next weekend in Azerbaijan, Shovlin added. He also expects Red Bull to make a step forward.

"I think if we hadn't had Monza, we would again be saying, Baku we haven't updated for a while, that's going to be a tough circuit for us. I think the fact that we showed that our car works well at these tracks that need low drag, we have an efficient car, we look good in a straight line, Red Bull are quite similar, and while that's not the only thing you need at Baku, I think if you've got that you're in with a decent shout and then we've got to sort it out for the rather twisty, wiggly bit through the castle and those corners.

"But we're looking forward to it and it is a track that George has been good there before. Kimi knows it now, it's not his first year and hopefully we'll be in a position to fight for a win," he concluded.

Entering the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Mercedes has a firm grip on the constructors' championship. In the drivers' standings, Antonelli currently leads his teammate Russell by 81 points .

articles.title: Ngetich new women-only half marathon world record holder
articles.summary: Kenya's Agnes Ngetich set a new women-only half marathon world record when she claimed success at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhage...
articles.body:
Kenya's Agnes Ngetich set a new women-only half marathon world record when she claimed success at the World Athletics Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.

Ngetich clocked 1 hour 5 minutes and 15 seconds as she finished 50 seconds ahead of nearest rival Veronica Loleo and also won the team half marathon rankings with her team-mates.

Ngetich had started 2026 with a comprehensive 42-second victory in Tallahassee to claim a first individual global title with a World Cross County Championship triumph.

The Kenyan long-distance runner backed up that win in the United States at the start of this year with an even better showing in Denmark.

The men's half-marathon was won by Sweden's Andreas Almgren in a European record 58:06 minutes. The European 10,000m champion prevailed five seconds ahead of Kenya's Nicholas Kipkorir.

articles.title: Rooney warns Man United are ‘too nice’, says squad lacks ‘nasty streak’ and dark-arts needed to scare opponents
articles.summary: Wayne Rooney has said Manchester United lack players with a 'nasty streak' and believes his former side are 'too nice'.Manchester United take on Fulham in th...
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has said Manchester United lack players with a 'nasty streak' and believes his former side are 'too nice'.

Manchester United take on Fulham in the Premier League this afternoon, aiming to bounce back from a poor run of results.

Michael Carrick's side have suffered successive defeats to Manchester City and Brighton in the league and cup, producing two meek performances.

United lost the Manchester Derby despite Phil Foden 's first-half red card for Man City, and Rooney said the differing profiles in the opposition sides were on show.

He praised the tenacity of City's summer signings in that game and believes United lack players who are willing to rile up opposition teams.

He added that his former side are 'too nice' and said opposition sides will have no fear of facing Carrick's side.

After meek defeats, Rooney says Man United need gritty, nasty characters to rattle opponents and fans

"[Man City] Bring [Iliman] Ndiaye in. Quality player, works hard. They bring Elliot Anderson in. Really good quality on the ball, but tenacious, puts his foot in," Rooney told The United Stand.

"He's a player that connects with fans. When you look at players you bring in, he's Geordie, passionate, wants to play every week. You can see that desire and that fight in him.

" Enzo Fernandez , South American, knows the little dark arts of the game. Plays in big games, real good character. I bet you he's a good teammate, and as an opposition someone that you hate.

"That profile of player is what we [Manchester United] miss. We miss players that will wind the opposition up, they will frustrate the opposition. They have got that nasty streak in them. That's what we miss. We're too nice as a team. I think opposition will come and think, I don't mind playing against them."

articles.title: What A Weekend For Football In The Triangle
articles.summary: NC State and UNC both had disastrous Saturdays
articles.body:
Other than Duke's solid win over an admittedly weak Stanford team, it was a dismal Saturday for football in the Triangle.

N.C. State's failure was particularly egregious and inexplicable: with the game in hand, up 31-28 with six seconds left to play, all the Wolfpack had to do was kill a few seconds to put Vanderbilt away.

They might have punted. At best, Vandy would have gotten one play, one Hail Mary pass. But Dave Doeren didn't make that call. Instead, he chose to play for a sacrificial safety. It would have been a one-point win, but a win is a win.

Unfortunately, State's quarterback, CJ Bailey, fumbled, and Vanderbilt recovered, giving them a shocking 35-31 win.

To rub salt in the wound, instead of Vanderbilt getting a Hail Mary attempt, State had one last play, but they couldn't pull it off.

Doeren has never been wildly popular with the State fan base, and this will certainly not help. Calls to have him fired immediately sprang up online. Wolfpack Nation is not happy.

With the departure of the toadish Will Wade last spring, and now this bizarre ending, it's clear that whatever demons are behind "NC State stuff" are not yet through breaking the hearts of the faithful.

The Tar Heels led 17-15 and were in the red zone late in the fourth quarter. After a long weather delay they settled for a field goal to go up 20-15, then gave up two touchdowns after that for another humiliation.

After the game, UNC coach Bill Belichick had to answer questions about the game and the investigation into UNC's program, and his son's resignation.

Well, he had to listen to the questions; he didn't really answer them.

We missed this column by Art Chansky , but this isn't the first time he has called for Belichick to be axed.

You know things have changed when Duke is the defending ACC champion and, so far anyway, clearly the class of the Triangle again.

articles.title: How Declan Doyle and Ravens Offense Can Attack Saints without Zay Flowers
articles.summary: With Zay Flowers sidelined by a hamstring injury, Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry and Baltimore’s receiving depth give new offensive coordinator […]
articles.body:
With Zay Flowers sidelined by a hamstring injury, Lamar Jackson , Derrick Henry and Baltimore's receiving depth give new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle several ways to attack New Orleans .

The Baltimore Ravens will get their first real test of the adaptability of new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's offense Sunday.

Baltimore ruled out Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers for its home opener against the New Orleans Saints because of a hamstring injury. Flowers missed practice Wednesday and Thursday, returned on a limited basis Friday and was downgraded from doubtful to out Saturday.

Flowers was the centerpiece of Doyle's passing attack in Baltimore's 41-23 season-opening victory over the Indianapolis Colts , catching five passes for a career-high 150 yards and a touchdown before aggravating the hamstring injury. He accounted for nearly half of Lamar Jackson 's 324 passing yards.

But Flowers' absence doesn't necessarily mean Baltimore has to find another receiver capable of producing 150 yards.

It may mean Doyle attacks New Orleans in an entirely different way.

And Doyle made it clear this week that adjusting to the personnel available is part of his job.

"Certainly, the availability of players – whoever that may be – shapes how you game-plan things," Doyle said. "I think that really is what being a good play caller [and] a good play designer is – being able to adjust."

Here are five ways that adjustment could take shape Sunday.

Start with Derrick Henry and make New Orleans stop the run

The most obvious adjustment is also probably the simplest: Give Derrick Henry plenty of work.

New Orleans allowed 165 rushing yards in its 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit in Week 1, while Baltimore ran for 202 yards against Indianapolis. Henry accounted for 144 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries.

That creates a matchup Baltimore can attack without asking any receiver to become Flowers.

Doyle showed in his debut that Baltimore's running game won't simply consist of handing the ball to Henry from conventional formations. The Ravens used unbalanced lines, multiple tight ends, misdirection and Jackson's threat as a runner to create favorable angles against Indianapolis.

Doyle was particularly pleased with the physicality he saw on tape.

"We want our tape to speak for itself – be playing violent away from the football [and] being high-effort players," Doyle said. "We were able to create a lot of space for our backs. We feel like our backs, if we can get them on safeties and corners, that is a good matchup for us."

Flowers' absence could make those concepts even more important.

Jackson also believes Baltimore's increased use of snaps from under center gives defenses more to process before they can commit to stopping Henry.

"They do not know if I am going to run it, [if] Derrick will run it. Is it a run play? Is it a pass play?" Jackson said. "It is a disadvantage [for the defense] each and every down, and we need that."

If New Orleans has to devote another defender to Henry and Jackson, Baltimore can manufacture favorable matchups for a receiving corps that suddenly looks much thinner.

Rashod Bateman should get his opportunity

Nobody has more to gain from Flowers' absence than Rashod Bateman.

Bateman went without a catch in the opener and was targeted only once, although another reception was erased by a penalty. But his quarterback expects the numbers to look different against New Orleans.

"My guy is actually going to get a lot more targets, I believe, with guys going down just because our offense is so explosive," Jackson said.

Doyle was already looking for ways to get Bateman involved against Indianapolis.

"I had a few plays in the openers that I felt like I wanted to try to throw the ball to him," Doyle said. "It just did not play out that way."

The coordinator also praised Bateman for what he did when the football wasn't coming his way. Bateman's blocking helped spring Henry's 32-yard touchdown run, something both Doyle and Jackson pointed out afterward.

Bateman doesn't need to duplicate Flowers' role Sunday. In fact, trying to make him do so would probably be counterproductive.

Flowers' quickness, yards-after-catch ability and versatility allow Doyle to move him all over the formation. Bateman can instead operate as Baltimore's primary conventional receiver and give Jackson a target on intermediate and deeper routes, particularly when play-action pulls Saints defenders toward Henry.

Bateman isn't worried about replacing Flowers' statistics.

"My time will come, and whenever that is, I will be ready," Bateman said. "I cannot be worrying about my stats. I need to be worried about how we can win a Super Bowl."

Use Baltimore's depth rather than trying to manufacture another Flowers

One of the central themes of Doyle's offense through the summer was versatility.

Now Baltimore gets to find out how much of it actually exists.

With Flowers out and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane on injured reserve following wrist surgery, Baltimore's available receivers include Bateman, Devontez Walker , Chris Moore , LaJohntay Wester and rookie Elijah Sarratt.

Head coach Jesse Minter doesn't want any of them trying to suddenly become Flowers.

"Just go out there and use the talent that you have been given and put it on display, within the framework of the offense," Minter said. "Not trying to go outside of who you are, man — just go out there and be you and run towards this opportunity."

That could mean spreading Flowers' responsibilities among several players.

Walker can provide vertical speed. Wester can be used on motion, screens and manufactured touches. Moore gives Baltimore an experienced, physical receiver who already produced a 53-yard reception after injuries hit the position against Indianapolis.

Jackson isn't worried about who gets the additional snaps.

"'Tay' [LaJohntay Wester], 'Tez' [Devontez Walker], Chris Moore, those guys are going to step in," Jackson said. "I have no doubt in my mind about our guys. They have been showing it throughout camp."

Expect more Mark Andrews and multiple-tight-end looks

Mark Andrews could be another major beneficiary of Flowers' absence.

The veteran tight end caught four passes for 49 yards against Indianapolis and remains one of Jackson's most trusted targets.

There is another reason Baltimore could feature its tight ends more heavily Sunday: personnel flexibility.

Multiple-tight-end formations allow the Ravens to emphasize Henry and the running game without surrendering the ability to throw. Baltimore can line up in a heavy formation, force New Orleans to match with bigger personnel and then send Andrews into the middle of the field off play-action.

Jackson completed 7 of 8 play-action passes for 128 yards against Indianapolis.

The threat becomes particularly difficult to diagnose when Doyle starts moving players before the snap.

"The confusion [the offense] is creating with the motions," Jackson said when asked why the new offense generated so many explosive plays. "They do not really know how to pinpoint a guy on our offense. This guy might be the strong suit on this play, and it isn't that. It [can be] any given guy."

Flowers was perhaps the most dangerous piece of that puzzle against Indianapolis, but the concept doesn't disappear with him.

Doyle simply has to use different pieces.

Don't abandon the creativity that made the offense dangerous

This might be the most important part of Baltimore's adjustment.

Losing Flowers could tempt the Ravens to simplify things.

Doyle appears more likely to do the opposite.

The Colts now have provided the rest of the NFL with a game's worth of tape on Baltimore's new offense, meaning the disguise and creativity that worked in Week 1 will have to continue evolving.

"The second that you are stagnant, you are [a] sitting duck," Doyle said. "People can start to game-plan you and attack you."

That philosophy could become particularly important without Flowers.

Baltimore can change personnel groupings, move Bateman and Andrews around the formation, use Wester as a motion player, send Walker vertically and force New Orleans to determine whether Henry or Jackson is carrying the football.

Doyle described the process as finding "the counterpunch" once defenses begin recognizing what Baltimore has already shown.

Minter saw the same thing in the season opener.

"What I really love [is] the scheme and the versatility that it creates," Minter said earlier this week, pointing specifically to Baltimore's ability to move its best players around and manufacture touches.

That versatility now gets its first serious stress test.

Flowers is Baltimore's most dangerous receiver and there is no obvious one-for-one replacement for what he brings to the offense.

Bateman can handle more of the traditional receiving workload. Walker can stretch the field. Wester can provide movement and touches in space. Andrews can attack the middle. Henry can force New Orleans to devote resources to the running game.

And Jackson remains the player defenses ultimately have to solve.

Doyle's challenge Sunday isn't finding the next Zay Flowers.

It's making sure the Saints can't figure out where the football is going without him.

articles.title: Who is Justin Bowick? Meet the WR who joined Oklahoma State football 'to be explosive'
articles.summary: Oklahoma State receiver Justin Bowick caught nine passes for 178 yards in the Cowboys' 59-0 win against Murray State on Saturday in Stillwater.
articles.body:
STILLWATER — Entering Saturday, it had been 676 days since Justin Bowick 's last 100-yard receiving game.

"It feels like forever ago," Bowick said. "It really does."

Saturday, the redshirt senior Oklahoma State receiver caught nine passes, a career-high, for 178 yards and two touchdowns in OSU's 59-0 win against Murray State . Bowick did all his damage in the first half, before the starters were pulled on the second drive of the third quarter. OSU (2-1) quarterback Drew Mestemaker looked for Bowick twice on the first drive, connecting on a 22-yard pass over the middle and throwing him a fade in the end zone that wasn't caught.

That opportunity is why Bowick transferred from Illinois to OSU in January.

"I mean, that's what I came here for to be explosive and get yards like that," Bowick said. "I'm very proud of that and it felt very good to have a 100-plus yard game again."

In November 2024 when he played for Ball State, Bowick had a 171-yard, one touchdown game against Miami (Ohio) and a 148-yard, two touchdown game against Buffalo the next week. After a career that started in the FCS level at Eastern Illinois because Bowick tore his achilles "off the bone" entering his senior year of high school, that breakout was his ticket to the big time of the power conference level. Bowick transferred to Illinois.

Last season, the Illini ranked No. 59 nationally in passing offense. Bowick played in 12 of Illinois' 13 games but didn't record more than 50 receiving yards in any contest. Bowick finished fourth on the team with 265 receiving yards.

Bowick said it's completely different playing in coach Eric Morris' offense at OSU, where quarterback Drew Mestemaker led the country in passing last season at North Texas and is averaging 294 passing yards per game this season.

Through three games, Bowick leads OSU with 281 receiving yards, more than he had all of last season.

"I mean, like I said, that's the reason I came here for coach Morris and his playcalling," Bowick said. "I've been loving it ever since I stepped foot on this campus."

Bowick has improved in every game this season. He made two catches against Tulsa, five grabs against Oregon and nine vs Murray State. The Murray State version of Bowick is the player he sounded like in fall practices.

Bowick, 6-foot-5, 209 pounds, generated lots of preseason buzz because of what his teammates said about his physical traits. He ranked No. 66 on The Athletic's preseason "freaks list" for a back squat of more than 500 pounds and 22 mph sprint speed.

"Freaky is definitely a word to use," OSU linebacker Isaiah Chisom said. "I think that's God-given. I think his athletic frame- he's a big-body receiver, so you definitely have to bring your A-game every time."

Saturday, receiver Chris Barnes didn't play because he was nursing a shoulder injury. Junior Wyatt Young made a highlight diving grab for a touchdown, but it was his only catch of the game. Aside from Bowick's nine receptions, no other cowboy caught more than three passes.

"And so I think he's having fun playing in a wide open offense, you know, in something where he's getting targets," Morris said. "And thought he did a phenomenal job today."

articles.title: Luke Littler threatens Dutch boycott after World Series booing
articles.summary: Luke Littler has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam. Th...
articles.body:
Luke Littler has threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The back-to-back world champion faced a hostile environment during Friday's win over home favourite Danny Noppert and it escalated on Saturday night as referee Charlie Costorphine had to intervene in the last-16 win over Nathan Aspinall.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

And he is "100%" prepared to do the same in the Netherlands.

"With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same," he told Online Darts.

"If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro tours over there. There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I'm getting booed.

"I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing, I've just walked off stage without thanking anybody. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

Despite the bearpit atmosphere, Littler came out on top in a last-leg decider with Aspinall to keep his dream of a clean sweep alive.

The 19-year-old is hoping to become the first man to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year, having triumphed in the first five.

Welshman Jonny Clayton awaits in the quarter-final on Sunday afternoon.
